title: Case Math Workbook
subtitle: Build Lightning-Fast Accuracy for Consulting & Finance Interviews

sections.title: Why Case Math Is Critical in Interviews

blocks.text: Consulting and finance interviews demand **structured thinking and numerical accuracy.** Even if your structure is brilliant, sloppy math can ruin your impression. Interviewers want to see:

items: Comfort with numbers under time pressure.
Ability to approximate without paralysis.
Logical step-by-step explanation.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Think of the last time you froze on a math question. What went wrong—panic, accuracy, or communication?

sections.title: Core Math Skills Every Candidate Needs

blocks.text: Before solving complex cases, master the basics:

items: Multiplication & division shortcuts.
Ratios and proportions.
Percentage increase/decrease.
Compounding growth.
Weighted averages.

blocks.label: Quick check
blocks.text: What’s 25% of 480? Did you solve it in your head or on paper?

items: A company grows revenue from ₹100 Cr to ₹120 Cr: growth rate = 20%.
If profits are ₹20 Cr on ₹100 Cr revenue, margin = 20%.
Ratio of fixed to variable cost = 2:3.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: A firm’s revenue grows from $200M to $260M in 2 years. What’s the CAGR?

items: Profit = Revenue – Costs.
Breakeven = Fixed Costs ÷ Contribution Margin.
Fixed Costs = ₹50 Cr.
Selling Price = ₹500.
Variable Cost = ₹300.
Contribution Margin = ₹200.
BEP Units = 50 Cr ÷ 200 = 25 lakh units.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Calculate breakeven for a SaaS firm with $2M fixed costs and $40 contribution margin.

items: Estimate taxi revenue in Mumbai.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Estimate annual toothpaste revenue in India if 4B tubes are sold at ₹50 each.

items: If price ↑ 10% and demand ↓ 5%, net revenue ↑ ~4.5%.
Bundling: 3 items for ₹99 instead of ₹40 each (₹120) cuts the price by 17.5%, which changes the margin.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: A firm sells 10,000 units at ₹500 each, and each unit costs ₹300. What are revenue and profit?

items: Example:
Revenue = ₹100 Cr.
COGS = ₹60 Cr.
Gross Margin = 40%.
OpEx = ₹20 Cr.
EBIT Margin = 20%.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: If revenue is $80M and costs are $68M, what’s the profit margin?

items: ROI = (Net Gain ÷ Investment).
NPV/IRR used in finance cases.
Invest ₹100 Cr.
Gain ₹140 Cr in 2 years.
ROI = 40%. CAGR ≈ 18%.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: A startup investor puts in $2M and exits at $3.5M after 3 years. What’s the CAGR?

items: A factory capacity = 100,000 units/month. Running at 75% → produces 75,000.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: A call centre has 500 agents. Each can handle 20 calls a day, and utilisation is 80%. How many calls a day?

sections.title: Common Shortcuts for Quick Mental Math

items: % of multiples of 10 (12% of 250 = 25 + 5 = 30).
CAGR = (End ÷ Start)^(1/n) – 1. For two years, take the square root.
Rule of 72 for doubling time: 72 ÷ growth rate.

blocks.label: Exercise
blocks.text: Estimate the doubling time at 12% CAGR.

sections.title: Practice set 3: Market sizing and capacity

items: A city has 10M people. 30% drink coffee daily, 1.5 cups each. How many cups a day?
A plant can make 1.2M units and runs at 70% capacity. How many units does it make?
A warehouse ships 12,000 orders a day with 60 packers. How many orders per packer?
A 200-seat plane flies 40 times a day at 80% load. How many passengers a year?
A hotel has 250 rooms at 72% occupancy and ₹6,000 a night. What is its annual room revenue?
Of 1.4B people, 25% buy a product twice a year at ₹250. What is the market size?
A machine makes 90 units an hour, 2 shifts of 8 hours, 300 days a year. What is its annual output?
A gym has 1,500 members paying ₹2,000 a month. What is its annual revenue?
2M households, 90% own a TV and replace it every 8 years. How many TVs are sold a year?
A plant at 60% utilisation makes 30,000 units. What is its capacity?
A PE firm invests $50M and exits at $120M after 5 years. What is the CAGR?
A project costs ₹50 Cr and earns ₹15 Cr a year. What is the payback period?
$10M invested returns $4M a year. What is the simple payback?
Using the rule of 72, how long does revenue growing 9% a year take to double?
At a 10% discount rate, what is ₹121 received in 2 years worth today?
Revenue of $100M grows 20% a year. What is it after 3 years?
A market grows from ₹400 Cr to ₹900 Cr in 4 years. What is the CAGR?
Capacity rises from 1M to 1.3M units while demand is 1.2M. What is utilisation now?
$5M grows at 8% a year. Roughly what is it worth after 9 years?
Revenue doubles from $100M to $200M in 3 years. What is the CAGR?

blocks.text: Check your working once you’ve tried each question. Rounded answers are fine in an interview if you say you’re rounding.
